response.title: which power stations can power a whole rv through the 30 amp plug
response.answer:
To power an entire RV through its 30-amp shore power plug (TT-30), you need a portable power station with enough AC output to run the RV's electrical system, ideally without limiting which appliances you can use.

The important distinction is that a 30A RV hookup provides up to 3,600 watts at 120V. Many power stations have a 30A-shaped outlet but cannot actually deliver the full 3,600W continuously.

What to look for

3,600W or higher continuous AC output: Ideal for supplying the full capacity of a 30A RV connection.

120V TT-30 outlet: Allows direct connection with a standard 30A RV shore power cord.

At least 3–4 kWh battery capacity: A practical starting point, though more is better for air conditioning.

Expandable battery capacity: Especially useful for overnight camping or extended off-grid stays.

A smaller power station can still power your RV through an adapter, but you'll need to manage electrical loads.

These models have a native TT-30 outlet and are capable of powering the RV's electrical panel.
